IEE Collaborative Research for the Digital Broadcasting and Multimedia Industries Seminar (Ref. No. 1998/416)
abstract: A new LINK Programme on Broadcast Technology was launched in 1997. The programme, jointly funded by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) has been set up to enhance precompetitive collaboration between industry and academia in advanced broadcast technologies. The government is committing #5 million to the programme in the first instance, and further funds may be made available once initial results from the programme have been assessed. Research within the programme will focus on three main areas: content creation; service delivery; and user interaction. The technical scope of the programme is outlined.

articleTitle: The Broadcasting VCE [Virtual Centre of Excellence]
publicationTitle: IEE Collaborative Research for the Digital Broadcasting and Multimedia Industries Seminar (Ref. No. 1998/416)
abstract: The Digital VCE is an R&D consortium of leading companies and universities working in fields of broadcasting and multimedia, a company limited by guarantee: registered as Virtual Centre of Excellence in Digital Broadcasting and Multimedia Technology Ltd., sponsored and supported by the UK Department of Trade and Industry. In 1995, the Technology Foresight Panel Report on Communications argued that the UK's research effort in certain key fields was unduly dispersed. The Report recommended that at least two Virtual Centres of Excellence be set up with government support, one in "mobile and personal communications systems", and another in "multimedia and digital signal processing". As a result the Mobile VCE and Digital VCE were established in 1996 and 1997 respectively, both with DTI and/or EPSRC support. The Digital VCE receives its core support directly from the DTI.

articleTitle: The Broadcasting Virtual Centre of Excellence: why the industry needs and supports it
publicationTitle: IEE Collaborative Research for the Digital Broadcasting and Multimedia Industries Seminar (Ref. No. 1998/416)
abstract: In order to explain why industry needs the Virtual Centre of Excellence in Digital Broadcasting and Multimedia Technology Ltd. (DVCE) we first have to look at why the broadcasting industry needs to do research. Clearly the issue of the natural convergence between the broadcasting, telecommunications and computer industries is a strong factor influencing any current economic model. However, in order to keep the discussion simple, we first develop a simple model of the broadcasting industry. This shows a simplified value-added chain for broadcasting. It is basically the process of how the general public's need for entertainment, information and education is satisfied by broadcasting-starting with raw materials, ideas and people. Similar separate diagrams could be drawn for the telecommunications and computing industries and indeed much more complicated economic models developed for how these services might interact in the future.

articleTitle: EPSRC programmes relevant to the digital broadcasting and multimedia industries
publicationTitle: IEE Collaborative Research for the Digital Broadcasting and Multimedia Industries Seminar (Ref. No. 1998/416)
abstract: The Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) acts on behalf of government to support research and postgraduate training. Its mission is to "promote and support high quality basic, strategic and applied research and related postgraduate training in engineering and the physical sciences, placing special emphasis on meeting the needs of users of its research and training outputs, thereby enhancing the UK's competitiveness and quality of life". This article gives an overview of the EPSRC's activities in support of the digital broadcasting and multimedia industries.

publicationTitle: IEE Collaborative Research for the Digital Broadcasting and Multimedia Industries Seminar (Ref. No. 1998/416)
abstract: The enormous costs involved in constructing prototype broadcast and multimedia systems, and the variety of specialisations which must come together in order to design them, have encouraged the formation of strategic research collaborations between organisations. Such collaborations are promoted through many national and international support frameworks which aim to stimulate innovation, education, technical standards, new markets and the acceptance of new technology by society. These frameworks encourage synergy and communications between projects, and usually award and administer the expenditure of research grants. The author believes, however, that insufficient attention within collaborative projects is paid to planning and management, with the result that a large proportion do not achieve their potential. Managers who are very competent at leading in-company projects often fail to recognise that collaborative ventures require additional skills such as: the choosing of partner companies, the division of effort, cross-cultural awareness, IPR strategies, company vs project allegiances and promoting healthy competition. This paper looks at some of the literature and studies which have been conducted in this area.
